title: Grain Clerk Training Note: The Grade Allowance on Foreign Material Struck on a Settlement Statement
content:
The grade allowance on foreign material under Grain Marketing Contracts is struck from the worst foreign material reading taken on every load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition, and where it arises it is struck on the bushels the statement settles.

**Where the reading is above 2.0 percent and the bushels the statement settles reach 1000**, the allowance is 0.03 per bushel.

**Where the reading is above the free foreign material tolerance the member's marketing programme carries but that pair of conditions is not met**, the allowance is 0.015 per bushel.

**Where the reading is at or below that free tolerance**, no foreign material allowance is taken.

## Which readings are looked at

Every load standing against the contract is read, whatever the disposition: a load the member directed to the contract at the scale and a load the member ran straight through to the buyer are both read, and the worst reading among them governs.

## The free tolerance each programme carries

| Programme | Free foreign material tolerance |
|---|---|
| Spot Cash Delivery Ticket | 1.0 percent |
| Forward Cash Sale Contract | 1.0 percent |
| Basis Fixed Contract | 1.0 percent |
| Hedge-to-Arrive Contract | 1.0 percent |
| Delayed Price Agreement | 1.0 percent |
| Minimum Price Contract | 1.0 percent |
| Managed Accumulator Program | 1.0 percent |

## Points of judgement

A reading of exactly 2.0 percent is not above the high ceiling, so it falls to the second band and takes 0.015 however many bushels the statement settles. A reading of 2.1 percent on a statement settling 1000 bushels reaches the first band and takes 0.03; the same reading on a statement settling 999 bushels takes 0.015. A reading of exactly 1.0 percent is at the free tolerance and takes nothing.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A hypothetical statement settles 4,000 bushels and the worst foreign material reading is 2.6 percent. Both conditions of the first band are met, so the allowance is 0.03 per bushel, being 120.00. Had the statement settled only 700 bushels, the allowance would be 0.015 per bushel, being 10.50.
